args.title: checkout-api: rolled back v3.1 -> v2.3.0 after failed health checks
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks following the latest production deploy of v2.3.1. Service status showed unhealthy across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0, the most recent version with a healthy production release history, in all three production regions. Rollback completed and verified (all regions reporting v2.3.0). v2.3.1-rc was noted as healthy but is a staging-only release, so it was not a valid rollback target. Please confirm service health recovery and investigate the v2.3.1 regression before any re-deploy.

trace.final:
Done.

**What happened:** checkout-api was on `v2.3.1` in all three production regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) and was failing health checks — unhealthy, error rate ~0.2%→ actually 18% at the time of diagnosis.

**What I did:**
1. Reviewed release history. `v2.2.9` and `v2.3.0` were healthy in production; `v2.3.1` was unhealthy. `v2.3.1-rc` was healthy but staging-only, so I excluded it as a rollback target — the task called for the most recent release healthy *in production*.
2. Rolled `checkout-api` back to **v2.3.0** across all regions. Verified: all three regions now report v2.3.0, health `true`, error rate 0.002.
2b. Note: this rollback targets a version previously healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was required. (Approval would only be needed to deploy a version that has never been healthy in production — e.g. pushing `v2.3.1` again.)
3. Opened incident **INC-0001** (SEV2, checkout-api) documenting the failure, the rollback action, and a request to investigate the v2.3.1 regression before any re-deploy. On-call has been paged.

One correction to my own summary above: the pre-rollback error rate was 18% (0.18), not 0.2% — the incident summary I filed states ~18% correctly.
